messages:
sara: Hey team — BrightLayer is seeing a sudden jump in p95 and a burst of 429s on their dedicated eu-west-1 pool. Customer says requests start failing after ~10s of normal traffic. They report MIG-level throttling events in our agent logs. Can someone triage?

eli: Can you paste the tenant/pool id and a short excerpt of the errors?

sara: Tenant=brightlayer-prod, pool=eu-west1-ded-3. Excerpt from their agent (sanitized):

```
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z WARN request_enqueue_time=0.312s tenant=brightlayer-prod route=/v1/generate status=429 reason=throttle
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z INFO mig_event=evict slice=1 node=gpu-07 reason=peer_saturation
2026-03-15T14:12:04Z WARN kvcache_miss_spike tenant=brightlayer-prod miss_rate=0.82
```

ana: cc @eli @mike — quick hypothesis: this looks like kvcache churn + MIG fragment bandwidth thrash. BrightLayer's workload is many tiny, short sequences (<=8 tokens) at high concurrency which keeps evicting prefix KV and increases DRAM/L3 pressure on certain partitions.

mike: I saw a similar waveform last month. Autoscaler didn't add slices because the dedicated pool is at reserved commit and burst policy was maxed. So it looked saturated but the scheduler couldn't supply extra capacity. Need to check pool scaling events around 14:10-14:16.

eli: Can we confirm packet counters / bus utilization on the node? If L3 or NVLINK bandwidth is saturated, we should see it in perf counters and MIG telemetry. Quick commands to run on the node:

```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,clocks.gr --format=csv -i 7
sudo perf stat -e L1-dcache-loads,L1-dcache-load-misses -a sleep 10
rdma-top -p
```

ana: Also repro steps we've been using: run our tiny-requests stress runner against a single slice in the pool with 200 concurrent clients doing 6 token prompts and inter-arrival 10-30ms. Script below — it reproduces the KV miss spike and then 429s within ~2 minutes on affected nodes.

```
# stress-smallseq.sh (bash)
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  (while true; do
    curl -s "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":6}' >/dev/null
    sleep 0.02
  done) &
done
wait
```

eli: Good. While reproducing, check the Redis kvcache stats and eviction counters too: `redis-cli info memory` and `redis-cli info stats`. We saw miss spikes in the logs (`kvcache_miss_spike`).

mike: One subtle thing — the pool's MIG layout: the node has 2x partitions per GPU (one 1g+7g mix). When lots of small workloads run, the 1g partitions saturate and cross-GPU traffic increases, thrashing the NVLINK fabric. We're seeing `peer_saturation` in the logs which matches that. Repacking to fewer, larger partitions may help but needs infra coordination.

sara: Customer asked for temporary mitigations — what can we do asap?

ana: Short-term: 1) Route BrightLayer to a GPU-variant with fewer MIG slices (larger partitions) if available in eu-west1. 2) Increase burst capacity for that dedicated pool (if allowed by commit rules). 3) Add a per-tenant rate limiter for tiny requests as an emergency throttle to reduce KV churn.

eli: I can flip a routing override for them to use model:rw-1-large-variant for the next 30 mins. Will monitor. :rocket:

mike: I'm going to check autoscaler logs now. If autoscaler suppressed scale up due to reserved commit, we should consider an autoscale policy change (min spare slices) for dedicated pools running high-concurrency short-seq workloads. Filing infra-ops followup.

deploy-bot: [alert] scale_attempt failed pool=eu-west1-ded-3 reason=quota_reservation_blocker at 2026-03-15T14:14:12Z

sara: Noted — customer appreciates the routing override. They also provided a small trace showing kvcache latencies peaked at 450ms.

ana: Owners: I'll take lead on repro and KV tuning. @mike please own autoscale policy followup. @eli please validate routing override and confirm no regressions. I'll open a reproducible issue with perf counters and sample load script.

mike: A few quick grep commands I'll use to gather perf data from the node: `journalctl -u node-agent | grep -E "peer_saturation|kvcache_miss_spike" -n`, `sar -n DEV 1 10`, and `nvidia-smi dmon -s u`.

eli: After routing override, I see reduced 429s for BrightLayer within 90s. Still seeing a p95 delta vs baseline but stable. Will keep monitoring and post updates here. :thumbsup:

sara: Thanks. Chloe from BrightLayer is on a call at 14:35 — I'll share these mitigations and the repro script. Follow-ups: ana -> reproduce + perf dump, mike -> autoscale policy ticket, eli -> routing override status.

(reacts: eli :thumbsup:, ana :thinking:, mike :eyes:)
